title: The Hidden Danger in Our Trash: Why Lithium Batteries Are Causing Fires
subtitle: Rising numbers of battery-related fires at recycling centers are creating a major safety and financial crisis.

summary.en: Recycling centers are experiencing a sharp increase in fires caused by lithium-ion batteries. These batteries are often found in everyday items like vapes, smartphones, and toys. Experts warn that when these batteries are crushed in waste trucks or sorting machines, they can easily catch fire. The cost of these incidents has reached an estimated £1 billion per year in the UK. Industry leaders are now calling for better disposal methods and new policies to protect workers and the environment.
summary.zh: 資源回收中心因鋰離子電池引發的火災急劇增加。這些電池常見於電子煙、智慧型手機與玩具等日常用品中。專家警告，當這些電池在垃圾車或分類機器中被擠壓時，極易起火。在英國，這類事故造成的年度損失估計已達十億英鎊。產業領袖目前正呼籲採取更完善的處理方式與新政策，以保護工作人員與環境。

paragraphs.en: A growing number of fires at recycling centers and in garbage trucks are causing serious concern for fire departments and waste management companies. According to The Guardian, these fires are happening at a rate of more than 10 every week. Experts say that the main cause of this problem is the incorrect disposal of lithium-ion batteries, which are found in many modern products such as smartphones, children’s toys, electric toothbrushes, and especially vapes.
paragraphs.zh: 越來越多發生在資源回收中心與垃圾車的火災，正引起消防單位與廢棄物處理公司的高度擔憂。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，這類火災每週發生超過十起。專家指出，問題的主因在於鋰離子電池處理不當，這些電池廣泛存在於現代產品中，例如智慧型手機、兒童玩具、電動牙刷，特別是電子煙。

paragraphs.en: The Environment Services Association (ESA), which represents waste management companies, shared new figures showing that its members reported 1,518 fires in the year leading up to March 2026. Out of these, at least 541 were directly blamed on lithium-ion batteries. However, the ESA believes the real number is much higher. A spokesperson for the group stated that while they know 40% of fires are caused by batteries, they believe the actual figure is closer to 70%. This is because it is often impossible to find the exact cause of a fire after it has destroyed the evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 代表廢棄物處理產業的環境服務協會（Environment Services Association, ESA）分享了最新數據，顯示其成員在截至二〇二六年三月為止的一年間，共回報了一千五百一十八起火災。其中，至少有五百四十一起被直接歸咎於鋰離子電池。然而，該協會認為實際數字遠高於此。協會發言人表示，雖然已知有百分之四十的火災是由電池引起，但他們相信實際比例接近百分之七十，這是因為火災發生後證據往往被燒毀，導致難以查明確切起因。

paragraphs.en: The financial impact of these incidents is massive. The ESA estimates that the annual cost of these fires has jumped from £150 million in 2021 to £1 billion today. Beyond the money, these fires put lives at risk and take a heavy toll on emergency services. For example, a recent fire in Ilford, east London, required 25 firefighters to bring under control. A spokesperson for the London Fire Brigade noted that these fires are very time-consuming and require a high level of resources to put out. They also highlighted the negative impact these accidents have on the local communities and the environment.
paragraphs.zh: 這些事故造成的財務損失相當驚人。環境服務協會估計，這類火災的年度成本已從二〇二一年的一億五千萬英鎊，飆升至今日的十億英鎊。除了金錢損失，這些火災更危及生命安全，並對緊急救援服務造成沉重負擔。例如，近期發生在倫敦東部伊爾福德（Ilford）的一場火災，就動員了二十五名消防員才將火勢控制住。倫敦消防局（London Fire Brigade）發言人指出，這類火災非常耗時，且需要投入大量資源才能撲滅。他們也強調了這些事故對當地社區與環境造成的負面影響。

paragraphs.en: To understand why this is happening, it helps to look at how these batteries work. Dr. Francesco Restuccia, a fire expert at King’s College London, explained that there has been a huge increase in these fires because we are using and throwing away more lithium batteries than ever before. He noted that if these batteries are not disposed of properly, there is a high chance they will catch fire. When a battery is crushed in a recycling machine or a garbage truck, the internal parts can be pierced. This creates an internal short circuit—a path where electricity flows in the wrong way—which causes the temperature to rise very quickly until the battery reaches its ignition point, or the temperature at which it starts to burn.
paragraphs.zh: 若要理解為何會發生這種情況，必須先了解這些電池的運作原理。倫敦國王學院（King’s College London）的火災專家雷斯圖恰博士（Dr. Francesco Restuccia）解釋，這類火災大幅增加，是因為我們使用並丟棄的鋰電池數量遠勝以往。他指出，若這些電池未經妥善處理，極易引發火災。當電池在回收機器或垃圾車中被擠壓時，內部零件可能會被刺穿，進而造成內部短路——即電流以錯誤路徑流動——導致溫度迅速升高，直到電池達到燃點，也就是開始燃燒的溫度。

paragraphs.en: The danger is particularly high with vapes. The ESA worked with the Health and Safety Executive to test what happens when a vape battery is punctured near paper or cardboard. In a video of the experiment, the vape ignited like a sparkler, reaching temperatures of more than 750C. This was hot enough to set the surrounding paper on fire for two minutes. The waste management company Biffa reported that it had recovered 500,000 vapes at its facilities during the summer alone, showing just how many of these devices are ending up in the wrong place.
paragraphs.zh: 電子煙的危險性尤其高。環境服務協會與英國健康與安全執行局（Health and Safety Executive）合作，測試了電子煙電池在紙張或紙板附近被刺穿時會發生什麼事。在實驗影片中，電子煙像仙女棒一樣點燃，溫度超過攝氏七百五十度。這足以讓周圍的紙張燃燒兩分鐘。廢棄物處理公司 Biffa 報告稱，僅在夏季期間，其設施就回收了五十萬支電子煙，顯示有多少這類裝置被丟棄在錯誤的地方。

paragraphs.en: These fires have occurred in many locations across the country, including Glasgow, Widnes, and several areas in London. Because of the frequency of these incidents, fire chiefs and waste companies are calling for urgent changes. The ESA is now suggesting a £5 deposit scheme on the sale of all vapes. Under this plan, customers would pay an extra fee when buying a vape and get that money back when they return the device for proper recycling. This would provide an incentive—a reason for people to act—to ensure that these dangerous items are handled correctly.
paragraphs.zh: 這些火災發生在全國許多地點，包括格拉斯哥（Glasgow）、威德尼斯（Widnes）以及倫敦的多個區域。由於事故頻傳，消防首長與廢棄物處理公司正呼籲採取緊急變革。環境服務協會目前建議，在銷售所有電子煙時實施五英鎊的押金制度。根據此計畫，消費者購買電子煙時需支付額外費用，並在歸還裝置進行妥善回收時取回款項。這將能提供誘因，促使民眾確保這些危險物品得到正確處理。

paragraphs.en: As the use of portable electronics continues to grow, the challenge of managing battery waste will likely remain a top priority for policymakers. For now, the message from experts is clear: lithium batteries should never be thrown into regular household bins. By keeping these items out of the general waste stream, the public can help prevent dangerous fires, protect firefighters, and save the recycling industry from a costly and growing crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著可攜式電子產品的使用持續增加，如何管理電池廢棄物將持續成為政策制定者的首要任務。目前，專家傳達的訊息很明確：鋰電池絕不應丟入一般家用垃圾桶。透過將這些物品從一般廢棄物中分流，大眾能協助預防危險火災、保護消防員，並拯救回收產業免於陷入日益嚴重的昂貴危機。

sources.title: Battery fires at recycling centres are costing UK £1bn a year, figures show

quiz.question: According to the ESA's estimates, what is the primary reason the actual number of battery-related fires is likely higher than the reported 541?

options.A: Waste management companies are intentionally hiding the true number of incidents.
options.B: The fire damage often makes it impossible to identify the original cause of the fire.
options.C: Many fires occur in locations that are not monitored by the Environment Services Association.
options.D: Fire departments often misclassify battery fires as regular household waste fires.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，ESA 指出雖然官方報告了 541 起由電池引起的火災，但實際數字可能接近 70%，原因在於火災發生後，證據往往已被燒毀，導致無法確認起火的確切原因。選項 A 錯誤，文中並未提到隱瞞數據；選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提及監控範圍問題；選項 D 錯誤，文中未提到分類錯誤的問題。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the potential effectiveness of the proposed £5 deposit scheme?

options.A: It will likely reduce the number of vapes being manufactured.
options.B: It will force fire departments to spend less money on emergency services.
options.C: It encourages consumers to dispose of vapes through proper channels rather than regular bins.
options.D: It guarantees that all lithium-ion batteries will be removed from the waste stream.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第六段提到，該計畫提供了一種「誘因」（incentive），讓消費者在歸還電子菸時能拿回押金。這暗示了透過經濟誘因，人們更有可能採取正確的回收方式，而非隨意丟棄。選項 A 錯誤，該計畫針對的是回收而非製造；選項 B 錯誤，這能減少火災發生率，但並非直接改變消防隊的支出方式；選項 D 錯誤，使用「guarantees」過於絕對，文中並未保證所有電池都會被移除。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, what does the phrase 'take a heavy toll' mean in the context of emergency services?

options.A: To require a significant amount of effort, resources, or cause damage.
options.B: To collect a payment for services rendered during an emergency.
options.C: To physically transport heavy equipment to a fire scene.
options.D: To reduce the number of firefighters needed for a specific task.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。「Take a heavy toll」是一個慣用語，意指造成沉重的負擔、損害或耗費大量資源。文中提到火災耗費大量消防資源，符合此定義。選項 B 錯誤，這與收費無關；選項 C 雖然提到資源，但該片語強調的是「負面影響或負擔」而非單純的運輸；選項 D 則與原文意思完全相反，因為火災實際上是增加了消防隊的負擔。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article?

options.A: The financial cost of recycling centers has become too high for the government to manage.
options.B: Lithium-ion batteries in modern products are causing an increasing number of dangerous fires, requiring better disposal habits.
options.C: Vapes are the only products that should be banned to prevent fires in garbage trucks.
options.D: Firefighters are currently struggling to find new technologies to put out battery-related fires.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。本文的主旨在於探討鋰電池（特別是電子菸）被錯誤丟棄後，在垃圾車或回收中心引發火災的嚴重問題，並強調大眾需要改變丟棄習慣（如不丟入一般垃圾桶）以保護環境與安全。選項 A 僅提到財務影響，不夠全面；選項 C 錯誤，文中提到多種產品含有鋰電池，不僅限於電子菸；選項 D 錯誤，文章重點在於預防而非滅火技術的研發。
